newsitem.title: USA: Swiss rail workers worked with Nazis -- documents.
newsitem.headline: Swiss rail workers worked with Nazis -- documents.

text.p: Swiss railway police collaborated with the Gestapo and daily handed over Jews, German army deserters and political refugees who tried to escape to netural Switzerland, according to a secret U.S. document released on Thursday.

The document, released by the World Jewish Congress, was written by a U.S. diplomat in Berne, angry at the failure of the Swiss in 1947 to purge collaborationist rail policemen who were helping Nazis in the postwar period to find a safe haven in Switzerland, and even feeding them in their canteens.

The diplomat, J.P. Robertson, the head of the American legation's economic section in Berne, wrote: "Nothing whatever has been done with regard to purging the railway police. Every one of them collaborated with the Gestapo and innumerable people were turned over to police by them.
"Jews and other politically persecuted persons, prisoners who wanted to escape in railway cars to Switzerland, as well as German soliders who wanted to desert were their daily victims."

He also complained that anti-Nazi railway workers had been dismissed for political reasons from 1933 onwards and even evicted from their homes. "They have passed through years of necessity, want and persecution and now (in 1947) must look on while Nazis are still in office."

Robertson also put into the records of the State Department a memo he wrote five months after the war's end in May 1945, naming 15 Nazi sympathisers in the railway police whom he declared ought to be purged.
They included a man who "ought to be discharged because he is an evil character" and another he described as "a bad character."

The WJC, which has been combing U.S. National Archives for documents on Germany's use of Switzerland as a safe haven for the assets it had looted in Europe, said it appeared that thousands of people had been handed over to the Germans by the Swiss rail police.

A January 1945 document from U.S. Secretary of Defence Henry Stimpson and U.S. Navy Secretary James Forrestal complained that the Swiss were allowing their railroads to ship war materials to German troops in Italy.

The memorandum, marked "top secret", was sent to the Secretary of State saying that urgent action should be taken through diplomatic channels, and suggested that if that did not work force would have to be used.
The documents were the latest among thousands found in the U.S. National Archives that show that Switzerland acted as a safe haven for Nazi gold.
Switzerland faces suspicions, fuelled by the newly declassified archives, that it could still be hoarding Nazi gold or holding millions of dollars in assets from people who perished during the war.
